title: Molina converts pole into Lausitzring Race 1 win for Audi
dek: Miguel Molina won Race 1 at the Lausitzring for Audi Sport Team Abt by 2.034 seconds from Jamie Green, retaking the lead on lap eight, while fourth place put Marco Wittmann top of the standings.

chapters.title: A bumpy track and a championship up for grabs
text: The DTM arrived at the Lausitzring on 4–5 June for the third weekend of its 2016 season, with Races 5 and 6 of 18 on the programme at a Motorsport Festival. Paul di Resta led the standings for Mercedes-AMG on 43 points after the Red Bull Ring double-header, where BMW had won both races: Marco Wittmann on the Saturday and Timo Glock, who started from third, on the Sunday. Edoardo Mortara was second on 40, with Maxime Martin and Glock level on 37. Mercedes had won only once all year, through di Resta in the second Hockenheim race.

BMW arrived expecting a hard weekend. Wittmann said the Lausitzring did not particularly suit the team, and BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt called it a track that did not suit the M4 DTM. The surface was a talking point for everybody all weekend: the circuit is full of bumps and hard braking zones, and Wickens said it reminded him of North America and demanded a very different driving style.

For Audi the weekend carried its own stakes. Miguel Molina had won only once before in the DTM, and Audi’s DTM chief Dieter Gass said the first two events of the year had not gone perfectly for the manufacturer, so a strong result at the Lausitzring was badly needed. Molina himself said the first two races had not been good for his team.

chapters.title: Molina takes pole, Wittmann springs a surprise
text: Molina set the pace early with a 1m16.619s, a lap that no one could match. It gave him pole position for Race 1. Jamie Green was the only driver to get close, 0.077 seconds slower in the second Audi, so Audi filled the front row. Green had struggled for balance in free practice and said the team had found a better set-up for qualifying.

The surprise was third place. Wittmann put his BMW M4 on the second row, 0.152 seconds off the top, and admitted that nobody in the team had expected it. Robert Wickens was fourth in the leading Mercedes on 1m16.792s, ahead of the Mücke pair of Lucas Auer and Christian Vietoris, with Mattias Ekström, Martin, Adrien Tambay and Nico Müller completing the top ten within 0.374 seconds of pole. Martin was eighth on the same time as Ekström, 1m16.901s.

The championship picture was shuffled in the lower half of the order. Di Resta, the points leader, could do no better than 21st, nearly three quarters of a second off pole, and started there. Mortara was 11th fastest but lined up 14th, and Maximilian Götz, 15th in qualifying, started 20th. Glock, the Red Bull Ring winner, qualified 14th and started 13th, Bruno Spengler lined up 15th, and Martin Tomczyk was last of the 24 cars on 1m17.536s.

chapters.title: Green leads, Molina strikes back on lap eight
text: Green got the better start. He took the inside at the first corner and slipped ahead of his Audi team-mate, while Wickens used a good getaway to pass Wittmann for third. A number of cars ran wide in the early skirmishing, but all 24 were still running after two laps.

Molina stayed within DRS range of Green and did not let him escape. At the start of the eighth lap he went down the inside on the brakes into the first corner after the start-and-finish straight and took the lead back. From there he steadily pulled clear, while Green had nothing left in reply and Wickens could only follow the two Audis.

Behind them, the race’s only retirement followed contact on the sixth lap, when Esteban Ocon’s ART Mercedes hit Tomczyk’s Schnitzer BMW. Tomczyk’s car did not continue, while Ocon carried on and finished 23rd, last of the classified runners.

chapters.title: Wittmann runs out of DRS but holds fourth
text: The fight for fourth took shape around Wittmann. The BMW driver had used up his DRS allocation early, and with the Mücke Mercedes of Auer and Vietoris closing in he had to defend the position on the straights without it. Auer tried to go around the outside at the first corner but could not make it stick, and Wittmann kept the place. BMW’s Marquardt later said his driver had defended like a lion.

Auer’s fortunes turned in the closing stages. With Wittmann still ahead, he dropped from fifth to seventh in the space of a lap, passed by his team-mate Vietoris and by Ekström, who had started seventh.

Further back, Mortara did his work in the midfield. He started 14th, brushed the wall at one point, and climbed to eighth by passing Glock, then Müller, and finally Martin. Martin held ninth, Müller took the last point in tenth, and Spengler missed out by one position in 11th. Di Resta started 21st and passed a string of cars to reach 13th, with Glock 12th, but neither scored.

chapters.title: Molina wins by two seconds as Wittmann takes the lead
text: Molina took the chequered flag 2.034 seconds clear of Green after 32 laps and 42m04.244s, setting the fastest lap on the tenth lap, and said afterwards that the car had been just as strong in the race as in qualifying. Green said he had not been fast enough for the win but was pleased with the points, and he named pole position as his target for Sunday. It was Molina’s second DTM win.

Wickens took the final podium place, 4.175 seconds behind the winner, after a race in which he tried to stay with the Audis and could not. He said Mercedes had deserved a podium. Wittmann was fourth, 8.724 seconds back and 4.549 behind Wickens, with Vietoris fifth, Ekström sixth and Auer seventh, so that Mercedes had three cars in the top seven.

Audi put five cars in the points, Molina, Green, Ekström, Mortara in eighth and Müller in tenth, including all four of the Abt cars. For BMW only Wittmann and Martin, ninth, scored. The result moved Wittmann to the top of the championship on 47 points, three clear of Mortara on 44, with Wickens and di Resta level on 43, Martin on 39 and Glock on 37.

facts.v: Miguel Molina won from pole in the #17 Audi RS 5 DTM by 2.034 seconds over Jamie Green in a race of 32 laps.

facts.v: Green passed Molina at the start, but Molina retook the lead at the first corner on lap eight and then pulled away.
Marco Wittmann’s fourth place put him top of the championship on 47 points, ahead of Edoardo Mortara on 44.
Esteban Ocon was given a drive-through for the lap-six contact with Martin Tomczyk, who retired, and finished 23rd.
